stories.headline: Man United transfer strategy 'financial sustainable' as losses increase - CEO
stories.summary: Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after reporting a increased financial losses.
stories.body:
Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after the club reported increased financial losses.

On Wednesday, United posted record full year revenues of £677.6m ($900m) and an operating profit of £22.6m ($30m).

However, the club still reported an overall loss of £43m ($57m), up from £33m ($44m) the previous year.

Borrowing increased by £95m ($126m) to a total of £583m ($773m).

United spent £155m ($206m) midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba in the transfer window.

Big six rivals Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea all spent considerably more with City, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea all spending at least £100m ($133) on one player.

And speaking as the club's fourth quarter and full year financial results were published on Wednesday, Berrada hinted at a need for a prudent approach to transfers.

"While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable," Berrada said.

"With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men's and women's teams during the summer window and our men's team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford."

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

- Mikel Arteta agrees a new long-term contract extension with Arsenal - sources

In the news release which accompanied the results, United said: "the club continues on its journey to improve operational efficiency and financial sustainability."

A United source said "stabilising the business has required, and will continue to require, hard work and financial discipline."

Among the expenditures for the year was £8.2m ($11m) paid to Ruben Amorim and his staff after the Portuguese coach was dismissed in January. United saved around £8.5m ($11.3m) after Amorim accepted the head coach job at AC Milan in the summer.

The club also paid off around £150m ($199m) from a revolving credit facility between March and June.

Meanwhile, United's finances revealed they paid £63.5m ($84m) for land associated with plans to build a new stadium.

Berrada said: "Our other main area of focus is our plan to develop a new 100,000 seater stadium. We have now completed the major milestone of securing the land which will form part of the proposed location of the new stadium."

Sept. 23: Wednesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action gets underway at 1:10 p.m. ET with an interleague affair in Motown. The Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals in a game between clubs playing out the string.

For the second straight day, a pair of teams will be taking the field twice, with the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles making up yesterday's rainout with a separate-admission doubleheader at Camden Yards. The good news is that Mother Nature should cooperate today, with early forecasts favorable everywhere. The bad news is that things could get ugly this weekend, with rain expected in the Northeast.
The Los Angeles Dodgers expect to have Shohei Ohtani serving as their designated hitter when they host the San Diego Padres this evening. Manager Dave Roberts indicated that Ohtani will be examined today and, barring a surprise, will return to the lineup. He's been convalescing on the 10-day IL, taking care of lingering knee and biceps issues.
Ceddanne Rafaela is expected to return to the Boston Red Sox lineup tonight when they host the Cleveland Guardians. The Gold Glove center fielder has been out for over two weeks with a right quad strain. Nate Eaton will return to his reserve role.
Ronald Acuna Jr. had to leave last night's Atlanta Braves game in the third inning after fouling a ball off his left shin. He was able to walk off the field with no assistance, and X-rays were negative, so the club is hopeful that he won't miss much time, if any. Brewer Hicklen finished Acuna's at-bat last night and would be the likely replacement if needed.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Wednesday.

Sept. 22: Tuesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Tuesday's schedule gets an early start with a doubleheader in the Bronx between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays. The opener gets underway at 1:05 p.m. ET, with the nightcap being part of the 15-game evening slate. The AL East combatants both have seven games left, with the Rays six games ahead of the Yankees. Winning just one game assures the Rays of winning the division and the No. 1 seed in the American League.

The Chicago Cubs announced Monday that 3B Alex Bregman will miss the rest of the regular season. He was diagnosed with facial fractures after being hit in the side of his face with a foul ball while getting loose in the on-deck circle on Saturday. The veteran does not require surgery, so he might still return to help the club in the playoffs. More will be revealed about his status later in the week.
The Baltimore Orioles pulled C Samuel Basallo from last night's game in the seventh inning. He was hit in the mask with a foul ball earlier in the contest, then was hit a few times with foul tips. The rookie has been the club's main backstop for just over a month, but he's batting just .158/.244/.250 over 25 games during that span. Carlos Narvaez will see more action if Basallo remains out.
In the same contest, Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Brett Bateman exited early due to a sore right hip. X-rays were negative, leaving his status as day-to-day. The 24-year-old outfielder is hitting a surprising .322/.393/.416, though with only two homers and three steals over 37 games. The Blue Jays were already playing without Vladimir Guerrero Jr. thanks to lower-back tightness. He is also day-to-day, with Sean Keys filling in at first base.
The Detroit Tigers placed Colt Keith on the 10-day IL yesterday, ending his season. The infielder's .258/.322/.406 final line mirrors last year's effort, with a tad less power but a few more stolen bases.
Reinforcements are returning for the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki both set to be activated before tonight's home date with the San Diego Padres. Pages is expected to be reinserted as the regular center fielder, shifting Tommy Edman to the keystone. Pages was out for over a month following surgery on a broken bone in his left hand. Before the injury, he was on pace for his best-ever season statistically. Sasaki missed almost a month due to a blister. He's slated to work out of the bullpen tonight, though his pitch count will be limited.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Tuesday.

Sept. 21: Monday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The final Monday of the regular season features only three games -- all evening games -- beginning at 6:35 p.m. ET with the Toronto Blue Jays visiting the Baltimore Orioles. A few minutes later, the Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals. The San Francisco Giants entertain the Minnesota Twins, closing out the truncated slate, at 9:45 p.m. ET.

Three teams have clinched a postseason berth in the American League -- all from the East. The Tampa Bay Rays are on the cusp of securing the division, with the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox ticketed to run back their 2025 wild-card matchup in the Bronx.
The Cleveland Guardians lead the Chicago White Sox by one game in the AL Central. The second-place finisher would be in the driver's seat for the final wild card. In the West, the Texas Rangers are one game up on the Houston Astros. The second-place finisher still has an outside chance at the last wild-card spot.
All three National League divisions have been clinched, with the Atlanta Braves ruling the East, the Milwaukee Brewers sitting atop the Central, and the Los Angeles Dodgers having nailed down the West. The Brewers have a two-game lead over the Dodgers for the best record in the Senior Circuit. The seedings for the Wild Card Series could go down to the end, with the Philadelphia Phillies just one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres. The Arizona Diamondbacks have not yet been eliminated, but they're four games behind the Phillies and a lot has to happen for them to extend their season.
The Blue Jays are set to activate Trey Yesavage from the 15-day IL to start tonight's road game against the Orioles, but they're aiming for only 45-60 pitches from the 23-year-old right-hander. He has been sidelined following meniscus surgery on his right knee and made only one rehab start, recording just two outs in that effort.
River Ryan is poised to make his first MLB appearance since 2024. He was acquired by the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal deal. The 28-year-old right-hander was shelved by a hamstring injury at the time but recently made two rehab starts for Triple-A Toledo. He'll handle a few innings before tagging in Keider Montero as the primary pitcher.
The Nationals will counter with DJ Herz, who has been recovering from April 2025 Tommy John surgery. The 25-year-old lefty threw 20 2/3 innings in rehab, the last 13 with Triple-A Rochester. He worked up to 65 pitches, so Herz could manage at least five frames if he's sharp.
Bryce Eldridge of the Giants has not been placed on the 7-day IL, but he nevertheless remains in the league's concussion protocol. The rookie is unlikely to play tonight against the Twins.

stories.headline: Lions make call on Neale Grand Final ban appeal
stories.summary: Brisbane will head to the AFL appeals board in a desperate bid to free suspended star Lachie Neale for the grand final.
stories.body:
Lachie Neale has faced a monster media pack on arrival in Melbourne as the star Brisbane midfielder appeals his suspension for the AFL grand final.

Neale remains banned for Saturday's premiership decider against Fremantle after failing to argue his way out of a one-match suspension for a gut punch on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan.

The dual Brownlow medallist gave a short statement after arriving at Melbourne Airport with Lions teammates on Wednesday.

"Very hopeful that it's successful, but regardless of the result, I'll be here to support the boys and the club," Neale said.

"It's a big week for the club."

Following the 15-second statement, Neale was chased by cameras as he immediately left the Virgin Australia terminal.

Fellow Lions veteran Dayne Zorko conducted a press conference after Neale's departure, with the majority of questions focused on the dual premiership co-captain.

Neale was also the story of grand final week last year, famously overcoming a calf injury to play a second-half cameo in Brisbane's demolition of Geelong.

"Lots of scrutiny last year about whether he'd play, whether he wouldn't," Zorko said.

"(20)24 he had a broken foot, so we're used to it.

"It's a lot (the attention), but he seems to be fine.

"I sat next to him on the plane.

"He's just taking it in his stride."

To succeed at an appeals board hearing on Thursday at 4pm, Brisbane will have to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

"There's been 10 (gut punch) incidents this year, all of them have resulted in a week (suspension)," the AFL's footy boss Greg Swann told reporters on Wednesday.

"That was the third (tribunal) appeal and they've all been upheld."

At the end of a four-and-a-half hour hearing on Tuesday night, the tribunal decided not to enact the 'exceptional and compelling clause' to allow Neale to avoid suspension.

Why? For many reasons, according to tribunal chair Jeff Gleeson KC.

There was Neale's evidence, which Gleeson rejected as "inconsistent".

Neale insisted he didn't strike Ginnivan during last Saturday night's preliminary final.

"We have listened carefully to Mr Neale's evidence but we find it was inconsistent in key respects with what we saw on the video," Gleeson said.

Neale maintained his shoulder and chest made contact with Ginnivan; the tribunal found it was "a forceful blow delivered with a swinging arm and an open hand".

That's the guilty part. Next was what Gleeson described as "the more difficult issue".

Was using the exceptional and compelling circumstances clause justified to downgrade Neale's penalty from a ban to a fine?

Introduced this year, the clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and the AFL's games record holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

But Gleeson noted Pendlebury was charged with rough conduct. Specifically, graded as careless conduct, medium impact, and high contact.

Neale was charged with striking graded as intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact.

Then, there was Neale's record, which his barrister - the AFL's former football operations boss, Adrian Anderson - compared to Pendlebury.

Until Tuesday night, Neale had never been banned in a 15-year career including two Brownlow medals, six club champion awards, and captaining the Lions to two premierships.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail preliminary finals: Yeo and Leota keen to stay Panthers
stories.summary: Isaah Yeo and Moses Leota are both keens to remain Panthers despite interest elsewhere, while Casey McLean is happy for his departing brother.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's preliminary finals weekend.

McLean opens up on replacing Crichton

Casey McLean has revealed the message from Penrith that helped ease the pressure of stepping into the centre position vacated by Stephen Crichton last year.

McLean admitted he initially arrived in first grade feeling as though he had to replace the premiership-winning centre, before being encouraged to forge his own identity.

"I walked in here thinking... I've got to replace Critta," McLean said.

"But coming here, the boys and coach, they're kind of just like, 'There's no shoes to fill. You've got to take the spot and make it your own, kind of play to your strengths.'

"'You wouldn't be here for no reason. You've worked hard... just be yourself.'"

McLean has since established himself as a key member of Penrith's backline as the Panthers continue transitioning into their next generation.

Leota disappointed to miss Warriors showdown

Moses Leota has admitted there was some disappointment in seeing the Warriors' season come to an end, denying Penrith a potential finals meeting with his former front-row partner James Fisher-Harris.

Leota retains strong ties to New Zealand and spent years forming one of the NRL's premier prop combinations alongside Fisher-Harris at Penrith before the Kiwi international's move across the Tasman.

"They had a really great season," Leota said of the Warriors.

"It's very sad, but it is what it is. There's some weapons in that team, right? They'll get back here next year."

McLean relishing Gagai battle

Casey McLean is preparing for another battle with veteran Knights centre Dane Gagai, declaring the 35-year-old is still performing as though he is in his prime.

McLean has previously spent time around Gagai in representative camp and has also faced the Queensland veteran on several occasions at NRL level.

"He's such an amazing guy," McLean said.

"I don't think he lets his age [affect him]... he still looks like he's in his prime.

"He's still running around, he's still doing what he's doing, leaving his mark on the game.

Yeo and Leota's future

Isaah Yeo has confirmed his preference is to remain at Penrith beyond his current contract, and is hoping to sort out his future following the end of the season.

"It always has been [my preference to stay]," Yeo admitted.

"The idea is to stay at Penrith as a one club player."

Moses Leota has also affirmed his love for Penrith, with the hope a deal gets done following the 2026 finals.

"[Remaining at Penrith] is massive to me," he shared.

"I've been here basically my whole life."

Casey McLean backs brother at Bulldogs

Panthers gun Casey McLean admitted while he's "gutted" that his brother Jesse will be leaving Penrith next year, but he's excited to see him flourish at Canterbury.

"Obviously pretty gutted that we won't be on the same team," he told ESPN.

"It'll be a weird feeling at first, but I'm super excited for the opportunity that he'll be given [at the Bulldogs]."

He went on to vouch for Jesse's ability on the field, expecting his older brother to remind fans of his talent.

"He does talk a little s--- on the field," Casey joked.

"But he's just an amazing player - he helped me grow as well.

"He's such an amazing role model, not only for myself, but for a fair few boys here as well."
